  1848		
  1849		Continuing from \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-9}, we use the first item of the Lemma which shows that $\| \ket{\Delta} - \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$ and equivalently $\| V_\alice^\dagger \otimes V_\bob^\dagger \ket{\Delta} - \ket{\hat{\psi}} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$, so 
  1850		\begin{align*}
  1851			\text{\cref{eq:qld-unitary-9}} &\approx_{O(\delta_S^{1/4})} \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\hat{\psi}} M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1852			&\geq 1 - O(\delta_S^{1/2})\;,
  1853		\end{align*}
  1854	        where the last line comes from \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-5}.
  1855		Together with \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-7}, 
  1856		\[
  1857		\text{\cref{eq:qld-unitary-7}} \leq O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)\;.	
  1858		\]
  1859		This concludes the proof of the second item of the lemma.
  1860	\end{proof}
  1861	
  1862	We now prove \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}. 
  1863	\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}]
  1864		Let $\strategy = (\psi,M)$ be a projective strategy for $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeeds with probability at least $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi}$ is a bipartite state on registers $\alice \bob$. As mentioned at the beginning of \Cref{sec:commutation}, we assume that the state $\ket{\psi}$ is padded with sufficiently many ancilla $\ket{0}$ qubits. Let $\phi_\alice$ be the following isometry mapping the register $\alice$ to the registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ where $\alice'$ and $\alice''$ are isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$:
  1865		\[
  1866			\phi_\alice: \ket{\theta}_\alice \mapsto V_\alice (\ket{\theta}_\alice \otimes (\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice' \alice''})
  1867		\]
  1868		where $V_\alice$ is the unitary acting on $\alice \alice' \alice''$ from \Cref{lem:qld-unitary}. Define the isometry $\phi_\bob$ analogously. \Cref{lem:qld-unitary} then implies that there exists a state $\ket{\aux}$ on registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ such that
  1869		\[
  1870			\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_\bob \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} \right \|^2 \leq \delta_\qld
  1871		\]
  1872		and for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1873		\[
  1874			\phi_\alice \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\alice \, \phi_\alice^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \phi_\bob \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\bob \, \phi_\bob^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''}
  1875		\]
  1876		where the $\approx$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$. This shows that $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ is a self-test for the strategy $\strategy^\pauli$ with robustness $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)$. We conclude the proof by making the identification of registers $\alice \alice'$ with $\alice'$ and $\bob \bob'$ with $\bob'$ to be consistent with the statement of \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}. We also note that, when unpacking the dependence on parameters $\eps, m, d, q$, the function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)$ has the form $a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for some universal constants $a > 1, 0 < b < 1$, as desired.
  1877	\end{proof}

    32	  \leanid{Real.pow\_div\_factorial\_le\_exp} in
    33	  \path{Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean} and
    34	  \leanid{Real.rpow\_le\_rpow\_of\_exponent\_le} in
    35	  \path{Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean}.}
    36	  The project packages these facts as an explicit polynomial--exponential
    37	  envelope and applies it after unfolding the canonical parameters and
    38	  soundness function.
    39	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} For a real exponent $s$, a rate
    40	  $t>0$, and $x\geq1$, put
    41	  $n=\lceil s\rceil_{+}=\max(\lceil s\rceil,0)$.  The Taylor bound at
    42	  $y=(t\ln 2)x$ gives
    43	  \[
    44	    x^s2^{-tx}\leq \frac{n!}{(t\ln 2)^n}.
    45	  \]
    46	  Its canonical specialization gives the explicit constant used to control
    47	  the third soundness term.
    48	  Tracked in
    49	  \href{https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-QPBT/issues/16}{GitHub issue \#16};
    50	  the parent blueprint task is \localissue{0002}.
    51	\end{itemize}
    52	
    53	\section{Key theorem forms}
    54	
    55	Let $a\geq 1$ and $0<b<1$ be the universal constants, and let $\eps\geq0$ be a
    56	failure-probability parameter.  The soundness function is
    57	\[
    58	  \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q)
    59	    = a(md)^a\bigl(\eps^b+q^{-b}+2^{-bmd}\bigr).
    60	\]
    61	Write $\log_2$ for the base-two logarithm and $\ln$ for the natural logarithm.
    62	For an integer $R\geq4$, let $c$ be the least even integer at least $(a+b)/b$, set
    63	$k=c\lceil\log_2\log_2 R\rceil+1$ and $q=2^k$, and let $j$ be determined by
    64	$2^j\leq c\lceil\log_2 R\rceil+1<2^{j+1}$. The remaining canonical parameters
    65	are $m=2^j$ and $d=1$. In particular,
    66	$m\geq (c/2)\log_2 R\geq\log_2 R$.
    67	The canonical-parameter lemma asserts that there are universal constants
    68	$a'\geq1$ and $0<b'\leq1$ such that, for every integer $R\geq4$ and
    69	$\eps\geq0$,
    70	\[
    71	  \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q)
    72	    \leq a'\bigl((\log_2 R)^{a'}\eps^{b'}+(\log_2 R)^{-b'}\bigr).
    73	  \tag{\texttt{lem:delta-bound}}
    74	\]
    75	For the third summand, put
    76	\[
    77	  n=\lceil a+b\rceil_{+}=\max(\lceil a+b\rceil,0)
    78	  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    79	  C=\frac{n!}{(b\ln 2)^n}.
    80	\]
    81	The required estimate is
    82	\[
    83	  a m^a 2^{-bm} \leq aC(\log_2 R)^{-b}.
    84	\]
    85	The constant $C$ depends only on $a$ and $b$.  This estimate, together with
    86	the source bounds for the first two summands, gives the asserted
    87	polylogarithmic bound for $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$ with $b'=b$ and
    88	$a'=a((2c)^a+C)$.
    89	
    90	\section{The source comparison}
    91	
    92	The canonical parameters are defined in \cite[lines~1503--1514]{Ji2020MIPStar},
    93	and the bound and its proof occupy lines~1520--1562.  At line~1543 the proof
    94	uses%
    95	\footnote{Tracked in
    96	\href{https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-QPBT/issues/16}{GitHub issue \#16}.
    97	The canonical parameter definition is at
    98	\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
    99	lines~1503--1514; the bound and its proof are at lines~1520--1562, with the
   100	disputed comparison at line~1543.}
   101	\[
   102	  2^{-bmd}\leq q^{-b}
   103	  \qquad\text{because}\qquad
   104	  k\leq m.
   105	  \tag{\text{source line 1543}}
   106	\]
   107	That comparison does not follow from the stated parameter choice.  For example,
   108	the allowed values $a=1$ and $b=1/2$ give $c=4$, and $R=5$ gives $k=9$ but
   109	$m=8$.  Thus the displayed justification is false even though the lemma's
   110	conclusion remains valid.
   111	
   112	The third term can instead be bounded independently of $q$.  More generally,
   113	for real $s$, $t>0$, and $x\geq1$, let
   114	$n=\lceil s\rceil_{+}=\max(\lceil s\rceil,0)$.  Since $x^s\leq x^n$, the
   115	Taylor lower bound $y^n/n!\leq e^y$, applied at $y=(t\ln 2)x$, gives
   116	\[
   117	  x^s2^{-tx}
   118	    \leq x^n2^{-tx}
   119	    \leq \frac{n!}{(t\ln 2)^n}.
   120	\]
   121	Now take $s=a+b$, $t=b$, and $x=m$.  Since $a+b>0$, the constant in this
   122	bound is the quantity $C$ above.  Moreover, $m\geq\log_2 R\geq1$ and $b>0$,
   123	so $m^{-b}\leq(\log_2 R)^{-b}$.  Hence
   124	\[
   125	  a m^a2^{-bm}
   126	    =a\bigl(m^{a+b}2^{-bm}\bigr)m^{-b}
   127	    \leq aC(\log_2 R)^{-b}.
   128	\]
   129	This is the required estimate with an explicit constant; no supremum argument
   130	is needed.
   131	
   132	\section{Comparison with the blueprint and formalization}
   133	
   134	The blueprint makes explicit the nonnegative failure-probability domain
   135	implicit in the Pauli basis test soundness theorem and otherwise retains the
   136	source statement.
   137	The blueprint proof records the Taylor envelope above as a separate
   138	formalization-support lemma and uses the same explicit constant $C$.
   139	
   140	The formal development proves the general envelope and specializes it in the
   141	canonical parameter calculation.  The canonical soundness bound is now fully
   142	proved, so no formal proof obligation remains; its additional nonnegativity
   143	premise is only the faithful domain condition on the failure parameter.%
   144	\footnote{The envelope is
   145	\leanid{MIPStarRE.LDT.rpow\_mul\_two\_rpow\_neg\_le} in
   146	\doclink{MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/RpowBounds.lean}; its specialization proves
   147	\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists\_deltaQld\_introParams\_bound} in
   148	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/CanonicalParams.lean}.}
   149	
   150	\section{Conclusion}
   151	
   152	The source's comparison $k\leq m$ is false for some permitted constants and
   153	values of $R$.  This is a local defect in the proof, not a gap in the lemma's
   154	statement: the Taylor envelope bounds $m^{a+b}2^{-bm}$ uniformly, and the
   155	canonical lower bound $m\geq\log_2 R$ supplies the remaining negative power.
   156	This replacement is now formalized and proves the source conclusion after
   157	enlarging the universal constant.
   158

    13	\title{Raw Pauli Effects in the Soundness Conclusion}
    14	\author{}
    15	\date{2026-09-21}
    16	
    17	\begin{document}
    18	\maketitle
    19	
    20	\section{At a glance}
    21	
    22	\begin{itemize}
    23	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The repair must control a positive
    24	  malformed-answer effect on the extracted ideal state for both players.
    25	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} Two rejection-mass estimates, two
    26	  completed-to-raw distance estimates, and one scalar-absorption step.
    27	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Matrix positivity, contraction, and
    28	  norm inequalities come from Mathlib and the quantum API; the oriented-edge

    30	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Completion changes only outcome
    31	  zero, malformed Pauli answers are rejected on a fixed Pauli--point edge,
    32	  and the robustness family absorbs linear and squared error terms.  The
    33	  repair is tracked by \ghissue{665} and its documentation by \ghissue{666}.
    34	\end{itemize}
    35	
    36	\section{Key theorem forms}
    37	
    38	Theorem \path{thm:pauli} compares, for each $W\in\{X,Z\}$ and
    39	$u\in\F_q^M$, the effect $A^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_u$ or
    40	$B^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_u$ directly with the corresponding ideal Pauli
    41	projector.  The same raw prescribed-answer effects occur in
    42	\path{cor:pauli-binary} of \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}.%
    43	\footnote{See
    44	\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
    45	lines~1426--1487, and the closing proof in
    46	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
    47	lines~1862--1876.}
    48	
    49	\section{Formal representation discrepancy}
    50	
    51	The formal game has one sum-type answer alphabet for all question types.
    52	Earlier soundness declarations first postprocessed a Pauli-question
    53	measurement by sending every malformed answer to the register value zero.
    54	For $u\ne0$ this completed effect equals the raw effect attached to
    55	\texttt{pauliOutcome $u$}.  At zero it is instead
    56	\[
    57	  M^{\mathrm{completed}}_0
    58	  = M_{\texttt{pauliOutcome }0}+M_{\mathrm{malformed}}.
    59	\]
    60	Consequently the old headline distance compared the completed family, not the
    61	raw family in the paper.  Rejection of malformed answers did not make
    62	$M_{\mathrm{malformed}}$ identically zero, so this was not a definitional
    63	identification.
    64	
    65	\section{Repair}
    66	
    67	For Alice, rejection on the oriented Pauli-to-point edge bounds the state
    68	mass of $M_{\mathrm{malformed}}$ by
    69	$|\mathrm{PauliEdge}|\,\varepsilon$.  The reverse point-to-Pauli edge gives
    70	the same bound for Bob.  If the transported strategy state is within
    71	$\delta$ of the ideal state, contractivity gives
    72	\[
    73	  \|\widetilde M_{\mathrm{malformed}}\ket{\mathrm{ideal}}\|^2
    74	  \leq 2\delta^2+2|\mathrm{PauliEdge}|\,\varepsilon.
    75	\]
    76	Since completion changes only outcome zero, the squared triangle inequality
    77	then yields, for each player,
    78	\[
    79	  d_{\mathrm{raw}}
    80	  \leq 2d_{\mathrm{completed}}+4\delta^2
    81	      +4|\mathrm{PauliEdge}|\,\varepsilon.
    82	\]
    83	On $0\leq\varepsilon\leq1$, the soundness function dominates
    84	$\varepsilon$; the existing scalar absorption estimates therefore absorb all
    85	three terms by enlarging only the existential prefactor $a$.  The usual
    86	monotonicity argument covers $\varepsilon>1$.
    87	
    88	The declarations
    89	\leanid{raw\_pauli\_operator\_distanceA\_le\_completed} and
    90	\leanid{raw\_pauli\_operator\_distanceB\_le\_completed} implement the two
    91	transfer estimates, and

    93	scalar absorption.  The public theorems \leanid{pauli\_soundness} and
    94	\leanid{pauli\_soundness\_qubit} now use the raw effects directly.  The
    95	completed-family distances remain as internal support for extraction and
    96	Naimark dilation.
    97	
    98	\section{Conclusion}
    99	
   100	The paper statement is unchanged and requires no additional hypothesis.  The
   101	formalization now proves its raw-effect conclusion for both players with the
   102	printed form of $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$.  The discrepancy and repair are
   103	tracked by \ghissue{665}; documentation follow-up is tracked by
   104	\ghissue{666}.

# Local operations — operator guide

This directory is the operative workflow of the repository: the local
replacement for the parent project's GitHub Actions layer. Architecture and
invariants: [`DESIGN.md`](DESIGN.md). Protocol changes: follow
[`protocols/meta.md`](protocols/meta.md).

## The lifecycle at a glance

```
issue  →  branch + worktree  →  agent session(s)  →  local CI  →  review
  →  (auto-fix loop)  →  merge gate  →  main  →  cache warmer refresh
```

1. **File an issue**: `local/bin/issue_new.py --title "..." --body-file b.md --label ...` opens
   a GitHub issue and prints its number; `--parent N` attaches it as a native
   sub-issue. Record each prerequisite, including one already closed, with
   `local/bin/gh_common.py add-blocked-by ISSUE PREREQUISITE`; the command is
   safe to repeat. The brief for the issue goes in `local/briefs/`.
2. **Open a PR**: create branch `issue-<number>-slug`, worktree under
   `.worktrees/`, run `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` there, then
   `local/bin/pr_open.py --branch issue-<number>-slug --title "..." --body-file pr.md --issue N` (the body follows the PR template in `local/protocols/issues-prs.md`),
   which pushes the branch and opens the GitHub PR.
3. **Dispatch agents**: only via `local/bin/dispatch.sh --role prover
   --issue NNNN --worktree .worktrees/<name> -- "task"`. Session telemetry
   lands in `results/telemetry/`. Lease-backed native descendants are retired;
   `protocols/sessions.md` retains their history separately.
4. **CI**: `local/bin/ci.sh PPPP` (build via hot cache + audits + blueprint
   checks) → per-step `local-ci/*` statuses and the manifest PR comment.
5. **Review**: `local/bin/review.sh PPPP` — runs only after green CI; publishes
   one exact-head COMMENT review plus the `local-review/summary` status.
6. **Auto-fix** (optional, the repository's auto-fix label on the PR):
   `local/bin/autofix.sh PPPP --mode auto`, capped, serialized.
7. **Merge**: `local/bin/pr_merge.py PPPP` — the gate; refuses on red CI,
   missing review, or unresolved findings, and merges via GitHub with the
   exact-SHA guard. Then pokes the cache warmer.
8. **Housekeeping / site**: `local/bin/housekeeping.sh all`,
   `local/bin/site.sh all`.

**Choosing the next packet.** `local/bin/ready_packets.py` walks the packet tree
under the Stage 4.3 tracker #47 — chapter trackers, their packets, and nested
chains such as Magic Square rigidity — and prints the open leaf packets whose
GitHub issue dependencies (`blocked_by`) are all closed. `--all` adds the
blocked packets with their open blockers, `--json` feeds the lane launcher, and
`--root N` restricts the walk to one tracker. Prerequisites live in those edges
only: the "Dependencies" bullets in a packet body are commentary
(`protocols/issues-prs.md` §1). A merged packet closes its issue and therefore
unblocks its dependents with no edit anywhere.

## Telemetry

Retired useful-work queue: [historical protocol](protocols/useful-queue.md).

Session, stage, build, and incident records live under `results/telemetry/` as
described in [`protocols/meta.md`](protocols/meta.md). The
[`design-decisions.md`](../results/telemetry/design-decisions.md) register is
the short, chronological index of owner and operator choices that shaped the
workflow; each row points to the longer primary record. Record reasoning in the
pointed event or owner log rather than expanding the index into a second log.

## Ground rules for agents

- Read `AGENTS.md` first; the faithfulness policy and proof-integrity
  blockers are unchanged from the parent project.
- Never run `lake update`. Never write to the hot cache. Full `lake build`
  goes through the machine-wide lock (`warm-worktree.sh`/`ci.sh` handle it).
- Publish branches through `checked-push.sh` (used internally by `pr_open.py`,
  `github-sync.sh`, and `autofix.sh`) so the gate finishes before push transport
  starts.
- One session never reviews its own diff.
- Worker sessions use `dispatch.sh`; the native lease and review transport in
  `sessions.md` are historical and must not be used for new work.
- Invoke workflow tools through the primary checkout's path
  (`/…/MIPStarRE-dev/local/bin/…`), never through a worktree's copy — a
  branch's copy can predate protocol fixes (EVOLUTION.md, 2026-08-30).
- After merging `main` or a stack parent, preserve every incoming-only path.
  The reference-transaction hook checks the exact merge object before the
  branch ref moves, while the pre-commit hook checks the pending index when a
  merge is committed later. Both run `local/bin/merge_loss_guard.py`.
  `merge_loss_guard.py --repo <worktree> --commit HEAD` audits a merge already
  committed by a lane whose branch copy predates the hooks.
- Friction with any protocol → log it in `results/telemetry/events.md`;
  propose amendments per `protocols/meta.md`.

## Declaring a track finished

The end of a track is gated like every other step of the lifecycle.
[`protocols/completion.md`](protocols/completion.md) is the definition of done
— zero proof debt, a built axiom audit over the headline theorems, terminal
paper-gap rows, marked or explicitly exempted blueprint nodes, a comparator
challenge pinned to an ancestor commit and naming every headline theorem,
truthful status docs, and the files an ITP artifact submission needs — and
`scripts/completion_gate.py check --track <track>` is the model-free checker
that decides the mechanically checkable part of it. No completion statement,
umbrella-issue closure or release tag without a passing run on the exact
commit. The gate is intentionally outside the blocking PR CI.
# Local Operations Layer — Architecture

This repository is a local-only continuation of the workflow that
[LionSR/MIPStarRE](https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE) evolved on GitHub while
formalizing the low individual degree test (LDT, arXiv:2009.12982). The active
track here is the **quantum Pauli basis test (QPBT)** from MIP\*=RE
(arXiv:2001.04383, primary) and NEEXP in MIP\* (arXiv:1904.05870, secondary).

Every GitHub-hosted operation of the parent workflow is replaced by a local
equivalent that *executes* here. Since 2026-09-01 the issue, PR, evidence and
merge **records** live on GitHub again (`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-QPBT`,
`protocols/issues-prs.md`); what runs is still local. The `.github/` tree is
kept **frozen as reference** — it documents the mechanisms being localized and
is never executed here. The operative layer is this `local/` tree plus the
(already-local) `scripts/` audits and `.githooks/` gates, which port
unchanged.

## Layout

```
local/
├── DESIGN.md          # this file — architecture and invariants
├── README.md          # operator's entry point: commands, lifecycle walkthrough
├── protocols/         # normative protocol documents
│   ├── meta.md        # how protocols evolve; telemetry duties (read first)
│   ├── build-cache.md # hot main cache; no-duplicate-compilation rules
│   ├── ci.md          # local PR CI gate
│   ├── review.md      # reviewer dispatch and gating
│   ├── autofix.md     # auto-fix loop, iteration caps
│   ├── issues-prs.md  # GitHub-backed issue and PR lifecycle
│   ├── sessions.md    # agent session naming, dispatch, archiving
│   └── EVOLUTION.md   # dated protocol-amendment ledger (research data)
├── personas/          # system prompts for locally dispatched agents
└── bin/               # executables (the workflow engine)
local/briefs/          # per-issue design briefs (committed)
results/telemetry/     # sessions/stages/builds logs, GitHub snapshot (committed)
```

Runtime state that must never be committed lives in `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/`
(hot cache, snapshots, locks, served site) and `.worktrees/` (gitignored). An
absolute `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` may instead hold branch-private `.lake` products.

## GitHub → local mapping

| GitHub mechanism | Local replacement |
|---|---|
| PR CI (`pr-ci.yml`) on push/PR events | `local/bin/ci.sh <pr-id>` run by the PR lifecycle scripts |
| Main-build actions cache (main-only save, PR restore) | Hot main cache: single-writer warmer + read-only snapshots + APFS copy-on-write clones per worktree (`build-cache.md`) |
| `lake exe cache get` (Mathlib cloud cache) | Unchanged — already local |
| Model-backed PR review chained on CI success | `local/bin/review.sh <pr-number>`: codex CLI with the same `.github/prompts/` review personas, invoked only from green exact-head CI statuses; one COMMENT review plus `local-review/summary` |
| Auto-fix workflows (CI-fix, blueprint-fix, review-fix) | `local/bin/autofix.sh <pr-id> --mode {ci,blueprint,review,auto}` with the same commit-prefix guards and a combined iteration cap |
| `@claude`/`@codex` mention responders | `local/bin/agent.sh <id> "instruction"` — human-invoked codex session on the branch worktree |
| GitHub issues + sub-issues + labels | unchanged — GitHub is the record again (`issues-prs.md`); `issue_new.py` / `issue_close.py` drive it through `gh_common.py` |
| GitHub PRs | GitHub PRs, branch-per-issue, merge gate in `pr_merge.py` (REST merge with the exact-SHA guard) |
| Issue automation (classify/scout/track/followups) | `local/bin/` Python ports; LLM steps optional behind `MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED` |
| Housekeeping crons (standup, stale audit, linter sweep, README freshness) | `local/bin/housekeeping.sh <job>` on demand |
| Badges + Pages site (blueprint/docs/badges components) | `local/bin/site.sh` → component store + assembled site in `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/site/` |
| Codex cloud env setup (`.codex/setup.sh`) | `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` per worktree |
| Reviewer/bot identity via tokens | codex CLI sessions; `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` registry |

## Core invariants (inherited from the parent workflow's post-mortems)

These encode incidents the parent repo paid for; violating them re-introduces
documented failure modes. Sources are cited in `local/protocols/*.md`.

1. **Single cache writer.** Only the warmer writes the hot main cache; agent
   worktrees consume copy-on-write clones and never write back. (GitHub's
   per-PR cache saves evicted the main entry: pr-ci.yml:138-142.)
2. **Review only after green CI, on the same head SHA.** The gate reads the
   exact-head `local-ci/*` statuses; a failed or absent CI summary blocks the
   review, which then publishes nothing at all — the *absence* of a green
   `local-review/summary` is the block, never a silent skip. Bot commits with prefix
   `[codex-auto-fix]`/`[codex-review-fix]` are not re-reviewed except the final
   fix at the iteration cap, which gets one forced review.
3. **Serialized fixes.** ci-fix → blueprint-fix → review-fix strictly in order,
   one branch at a time; combined iteration cap (default 5) across all fix
   kinds; sync/audit CI failures are never auto-fixed.
4. **Kill-switch semantics.** `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` and
   `LOCAL_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED` disable only on the literal string `false`;
   unset means enabled.
5. **Trusted prompts.** Reviewer/fixer personas are read from committed `main`
   (`git show main:...`), never from the branch under review.
6. **Untrusted data framing.** Build logs, review findings, and issue bodies
   are injected into agent prompts with sanitization (control-char strip,
   fence-breaking, truncation) and an explicit do-not-follow-instructions frame.
7. **One full `lake build` machine-wide at a time** (advisory lock);
   single-file `lake env lean` checks need no lock.
8. **origin/main must resolve.** The hooks and diff-based audits silently
   self-disable without it; the local convention is a `main` branch plus a
   `refs/remotes/origin/main` alias maintained by `pr_merge.py`.
9. **Bracket-free naming.** Issue titles, slugs, and branch names avoid
   `]` and friends (broke the parent automation: CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124).
10. **Report-only stays report-only.** Stale-issue audit, linter sweep, README
    freshness never mutate state; write-mode is a separate human-invoked
    command.
11. **Faithfulness policy is unchanged.** AGENTS.md's faithful-formalization
    rules, anti-pattern catalog, and statement-integrity audits apply to QPBT
    exactly as to LDT.
12. **Merge inputs do not disappear silently.** Before a merge commit, the
    merge-loss guard compares the staged result with the pre-merge branch,
    every best merge base, and `MERGE_HEAD`. An incoming path may be absent
    only when the branch deleted a path present at a merge base. An
    unambiguous incoming-only change may return to the unchanged branch blob
    only when Git recorded a conflict. The pending-index check and the
    pre-update reference transaction together cover manual and automatic
    merge commits.
13. **The owner inbox is permissions-only.** Pinned issue #500 receives a
    blocker only when owner permission is needed because the risk extends
    beyond project development, such as owner files, the machine or its
    accounts, spending money, or action outside this repository. Main decides
    and records every question whose only risk is failure to finish the
    project. Changing the stated project goal is outside main's authority and
    requires an owner decision on #500. Each blocker is one comment with at
    most ten visible plain-language lines: what is stuck, lettered options,
    one recommendation, and the literal `DECISION B<n>: <letter>` reply. Ids
    continue after B11;
    details are folded. Its immutable `<!-- owner-inbox id=B<n> -->` identity
    marker keys every `ensure-pr-comment` update; resolution changes the
    separate status field to `<!-- owner-inbox-status=closed -->` and adds
    `RESOLVED B<n>`. Issue #26 is archived and receives no new traffic.

## Naming and identity conventions

- **Issues and PRs**: GitHub's, identified by their numbers; sub-issues carry
  the parent/child structure and repository labels are the taxonomy
  (`issues-prs.md`). PR bodies keep the Motivation/Description/Testing shape of
  CONTRIBUTING.md; evidence is exact-head commit statuses, the manifest comment
  and the COMMENT review.
- **Branches**: `issue-<number>-<slug>` (orchestrator/human),
  `codex/issue-<number>-<slug>` (agent-created); the number is the GitHub
  issue's.
- **Fix commits**: `autofix.sh`'s subjects are prefixed `[codex-auto-fix]` /
  `[codex-review-fix]` exactly (the review-gate skip regex depends on them);
  operator and worker repairs use plain `fix(...)` subjects and are reviewed.
- **Codex sessions**: `<role>-<issue|scope>-<yyyymmdd>-<seq>` with roles
  `orc, prover, reviewer, simplifier, blueprint, splitter, scout`, plus
  `mathfix` for Astra source-statement repair under `issues-prs.md` section 6.
  External sessions use `local/bin/dispatch.sh`, which records the codex `thread_id`,
  captures the `--json` event stream to
  `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl`, and appends a summary line to
  `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`. Archiving a session = final status line
  in the registry + worktree removal; the JSONL capture is the archive.
  Historical native-descendant rows remain readable, but lease-backed native
  dispatch is retired (`sessions.md`, issue #505).

## Telemetry (research-paper data)

All appends are one-line JSON; schemas documented in `protocols/meta.md`.

- `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` — one line per agent session: name, role,
  selected account and model, effective requested effort (all optional on legacy
  rows), issue/pr, thread_id, start/end, wall seconds, token usage (input,
  cached, output, reasoning), exit status, dispatcher. Requested effort is a CLI
  input, not provider-measured effort.
- `results/telemetry/stages.jsonl` — one line per project stage/substage
  transition with timestamps and manual token/agent tallies.
- `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl` — one line per full build / cache event:
  kind (warm, rebuild, cache-get), duration, outcome, trigger.
- `results/telemetry/events.md` — dated free-form incident log (what broke,
  diagnosis, fix); the raw feed for `protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.
- `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md` — dated protocol amendments: cause (cite an
  `events.md` entry or telemetry), the change, expected effect. This file is
  the primary record of workflow self-evolution.

## Model policy

- Main remains `gpt-6-astra`/`ultra`. Published `local/model-policy.json`
  selects exact `gpt-5.6-sol`/`ultra` for routine/bounded subagents, including
  routine independent reviewers; genuinely hard/escalated work uses Astra with
  an explicit reason. Unknown classes/models and other efforts fail closed.
  External dispatch keeps fan-out off. Native lease admission and the useful queue
  are retired (#505). Worker reservations use only the two configured account caps;
  missing caps disable admission. They do not measure provider throughput or unmarked use.
- See `protocols/sessions.md` for marker accounting, resume affinity and checkpoint
  continuations. Historical Sol/Fable measurements are unchanged.
- Reviewer and prover roles must be **different sessions** — a session never
  reviews its own diff.

    62	Under the paper's global convention, the displayed polynomial assertion means
    63	that there is a universal $C>0$ such that
    64	\[
    65	  \delta_{\mathrm{pasting}}(\eta,\delta) \leq C(\eta\delta)^C
    66	  \qquad (\eta,\delta>0).
    67	  \tag{product contract}
    68	\]
    69	The imported proof instead accumulates terms depending separately on the two
    70	errors, including $O(\delta^{1/2})$, $O((\delta+\eta)^{1/2})$, and $\eta$.
    71	A compatible corrected theorem form would use, for example, an upper bound by
    72	$A(\eta^r+\delta^s)$ for universal $A\geq1$ and $r,s>0$.
    73	The polynomial shorthand itself is only an upper bound on positive inputs;
    74	it supplies neither axis values nor an additional nonnegativity condition.
    75	The corrected predicate supplies both on the closed nonnegative quadrant.
    76	
    77	\section{The source assertion}
    78	
    79	Lemma~\texttt{lem:pasting} of \cite[lines~504--525]{Ji2020MIPStar} imports
    80	Fact~4.35 from the NEEXP paper.  Its error is declared to be
    81	$\operatorname{poly}(\eta,\delta)$.  The asymptotic convention in
    82	\cite[lines~19--29]{Ji2020MIPStar} requires every variable to occur in the
    83	product on the right side of the product contract.  The proof of the imported
    84	fact, however, bounds the two sources of error independently; see
    85	\cite[lines~1030--1209]{Natarajan2018NEEXP}.%
    86	\footnote{The mirrored passages are
    87	\path{references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex}, lines~19--29;
    88	\path{references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex}, lines~504--525;
    89	and \path{references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex},
    90	lines~1030--1209.}
    91	
    92	More explicitly, fix a probability distribution $\mathcal D$ on
    93	$(x,y_1,y_2)$, a unit bipartite state $\psi$, and nonnegative $\eta,\delta$.
    94	Let $G_i^x$ be measurements indexed by functions
    95	$g_i:\mathcal Y_i\to\mathcal R_i$, with $G_2^x$ projective, and let
    96	$A^{x,y_1,y_2}$ be a projective joint answer measurement. Assume that distinct
    97	second codewords agree with conditional probability at most $\eta$, given
    98	$(x,y_1)$ whenever this conditioning has positive probability. Write
    99	$Q_{i,a_i}=(G_i)^x_{[\operatorname{eval}_{y_i}(\cdot)=a_i]}$.
   100	The input comparisons, averaged over $\mathcal D$, are
   101	\begin{equation}\label{eq:pasting-1}
   102	 A^{x,y_1,y_2}_{a_i}\ot\mathrm{Id}
   103	 \simeq_\delta\mathrm{Id}\ot Q_{i,a_i}\quad(i=1,2),
   104	\end{equation}
   105	\begin{equation}\label{eq:pasting-2}
   106	 A^{x,y_1,y_2}_{a_1,a_2}\ot\mathrm{Id}
   107	 \simeq_\delta\mathrm{Id}\ot A^{x,y_1,y_2}_{a_1,a_2}.
   108	\end{equation}
   109	Define $J^x_{g_1,g_2}=(G_2)^x_{g_2}(G_1)^x_{g_1}(G_2)^x_{g_2}$.
   110	The asserted universal function $\delta_{\mathrm{pasting}}$ bounds
   111	\begin{equation}\label{eq:pasting-3}
   112	 A^{x,y_1,y_2}_{a_1,a_2}\ot\mathrm{Id}
   113	 \simeq_{\delta_{\mathrm{pasting}}(\eta,\delta)}
   114	 \mathrm{Id}\ot J^x_{[g_1(y_1)=a_1,\,g_2(y_2)=a_2]}.
   115	\end{equation}

\[

### Selected target

The selected quantitative calculation is

\[
 \boxed{
 B_{\mathrm{QPBT}}
 =\min\{4,10^{14}(md)^4E_b\},
 \qquad b=\frac1{67108864}.}
\]

It is intended to yield the canonical corollary

\[
 \boxed{\Delta_{100,\,1/67108864}(\varepsilon,m,d,q)}
\]

and the corresponding qubit form by the existing exact unitary transport. The
degree four estimate is the sharper quantitative statement; `a = 100` is a
convenient canonical presentation, not an optimized degree.

The exponent improves by

\[
 \frac{5242880000}{67108864}=78.125.
\]

This is **one QPBT implementation scope**. It has three inseparable ingredients:

1. import the selected LDT theorem into the live one-coordinate direct
   low-degree theorem without the current extra square root;
2. keep numerical coefficients separate from polynomial degrees through the
   point, line, rounding, and global-pair estimates;
3. retain the stronger state estimate separately from the squared operator
   estimates through extraction, Naimark reduction, and raw-answer transfer.

This scope does not authorize the deferred commutation, pasting, or rounding
changes listed below.

#### The live low-degree route

The QPBT headline uses the one-coordinate theorem
`exists_direct_ld_soundness_of_k_eq_one`, not the general simultaneous theorem
or the seed-indexed theorem `exists_ld_soundness`. In this application, the
direct-game simultaneity parameter equals one, while the inherited LDT sampling
parameter is

\[
 N=2560000M^3d.
\]

Applying the selected LDT estimate at \(\tau=1/8192\) gives a one-coordinate
bound that fits \(\delta_{\mathrm{LD}}(30,\tau)\) after using the unit cap. This
avoids the square root introduced only to reuse the older general scalar
helper.

The distinction from other nearby theorems is important. The general direct
transport and the seed-indexed theorem are valid, but they are off the Pauli
headline route. Similarly, the full Magic Square rigidity theorem with
coefficient \(2\cdot10^{12}\) is not the quantitative input used by Pauli
commutation. The live path uses the direct original-state anticommutator bound
\(1183680\varepsilon\). The combined-point construction also uses a
field-valued sandwich measurement and projective rounding, rather than the
separately proved quantum-linearity theorem.

#### Retaining the existing stronger estimates

At the extended dimension \(M=2m+2\le4m\), the existing passing calculation
gives, on the small-parameter branch,

\[
 T_{\mathrm{pass}}
 \le10^8m\bigl(e^{1/512}+r^{1/32}\bigr).
\]

Set

\[
 u=\frac{1}{4194304},\qquad v=\frac{1}{33554432}.
\]

The direct low-degree and rounding estimates then give

\[
 \delta\le10^{22}n^{32}E_u,
 \qquad
 g\le10^7n^4E_v.
\]

For extraction, put

\[
 x=2800(g+\sqrt e+r).
\]

The existing construction already supplies one normalized auxiliary state for
which

\[
 s^2\le16x,
 \qquad
 D_{\mathrm{swap}}\le2x+2r+16\sqrt x.
\]

These estimates should remain attached to the same auxiliary state instead of
being enlarged immediately to a common fourth-root error. The current transfer
inequalities then give

\[
 \begin{aligned}
 D_{\mathrm{isometry}}
  &\le36x+4r+32\sqrt x,\\
 D_{\mathrm{Naimark}}
  &\le204x+12r+96\sqrt x,\\
 D_{\mathrm{raw}}
  &\le472x+24r+192\sqrt x+344e.
 \end{aligned}
\]

Since \(x\le10^{11}n^4E_v\), root subadditivity and exponent monotonicity
give, with \(b=v/2\),

\[
 s,\ D_{\mathrm{raw}}\le10^{14}n^4E_b.
\]

The full-domain proof uses \(e=\min(\varepsilon,1)\) and the independent
trivial bounds: a difference of unit states has norm at most two, and each raw
operator-family distance is at most four. The cases \(r\ge1\) and \(n=1\)
already make the proposed envelope at least four. Zero error is supported, and
no divisibility condition on \(2m+2\) is introduced.

The final theorem must retain the source-facing **raw prescribed-answer
effects**, not only the internally completed Pauli measurements. It must also
retain the range projections used by the existing isometry and Naimark
arguments.

## Comparison with the pinned public `qldErr`

### Source and domain

The benchmark is Thomas Vidick's public `MIPRE-formalization` at exact commit
[`286b3ca44f811fa6e37517c04981bc2f164ee6b5`][public-commit]. The inspected
mirror contained 398 manifested source files, all of whose hashes matched its
provenance record. The pinned repository license is
[Apache-2.0][public-license]. No benchmark code was copied, and no benchmark
build was run for this report.

The public theorem [`qld_soundness`][public-soundness] covers arbitrary POVM
strategies. The construction of the mirror witness is present in
[`MirrorExists.lean`][public-mirror], and the divisibility \(4m\mid q\) needed
inside the small-error regime is derived in [`Regime.lean`][public-regime]. An
earlier preliminary concern that either piece was missing is therefore
superseded. Likewise, a suspected square-root mismatch in `deltaLegs_comp` was a
parsing error; the proof and definition agree. Neither concern is a defect of
the public repository.

The public theorem ranges over arbitrary finite fields of characteristic two.
The local theorem uses the fixed admissible field model with \(q=2^\ell\) for
odd \(\ell\), \(d\ge1\), and \(m\mid q\). Numerical comparisons below are on
the shared domain.

### The actual capped composition

The public error is a composed function, not merely an existential slogan. With
the notation \(e,n,r\) above, define

\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_V&=2\sqrt{57676416e}+\sqrt{86e}+86e,\\
 D_V&=80Q_V+9228227936e,\\
 P_V&=D_V/2+\sqrt{D_V/2}
  +\sqrt{32D_V+4\sqrt{172e}+2(n+1)/q},\\
 T_V&=5m^2P_V+4Q_V+(n+1)/q,\\
 A_V^{\mathrm{CL}}&=2\cdot10^{11},
 \qquad B_V^{\mathrm{CL}}=1/40000,\\
 L_V&=A_V^{\mathrm{CL}}(4n)^{A_V^{\mathrm{CL}}}
 \left(T_V^{B_V^{\mathrm{CL}}}+q^{-B_V^{\mathrm{CL}}}
 +2^{-4B_V^{\mathrm{CL}}n}\right),\\
 +2^{-4B_V^{\mathrm{CL}}n}\right),\\
 U_V&=2L_V+115352832e,\\
 S_V&=2\sqrt{U_V}+2/q+8U_V,\\
 X_V&=72(10S_V+860e+2\sqrt{172e}+r),\\
 H_V&=2\sqrt{X_V}+2X_V,
 \qquad \eta_V=2-2\sqrt{1-H_V},\\
 F_V&=66S_V+44\sqrt{688e}+46r+1892e+13\sqrt{\eta_V}.
 \end{aligned}
\]

The definition in [`QLDError.lean`][public-qlderr] is

\[
 \operatorname{qldErr}(e,m,d,q)=
 \begin{cases}
 \min(F_V,4),&48n\le q\text{ and }H_V<1,\\
 4,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]

The component definitions occur in the public files
[`Combined.lean`][public-combined], [`Lines.lean`][public-lines],
[`PaddedLIDT.lean`][public-padded], the classical LDT
[`Parameters.lean`][public-lidt-parameters], [`SwapItemOne.lean`][public-swap-one],
and [`SwapItemTwo.lean`][public-swap-two].

### Existential witness and sharper calculated envelope

The public theorem [`exists_qldErr_le`][public-qlderr-witness] existentially
bounds `qldErr` by the same shape \(\Delta_{a,b}\). Reconstructing the witness
arithmetic used by that proof gives

\[
 b_V=\frac1{2560000}.
\]

If \(A=2\cdot10^{11}\) and

\[
 R=(A4^A+1)(A+9456574485125),
\]

then the traced coefficient parameter is

\[
 \boxed{a_V=10758960R+620538301950748.}
\]

It has \(\log_{10}a_V\approx120411998296.91\). These are reconstructed proof
witnesses, not numbers printed in the existential theorem.

A separate calculation from the definitions avoids the initial weakening
\(e\le e^{1/2}\) in the generic error-shape argument and gives the sharper
**unformalized scalar envelope**

\[
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{qldErr}(e,m,d,q)
 \le\min\!\left(4,\Delta_{10^{12},\,1/1280000}
   (\varepsilon,m,d,q)\right).}
\]

This envelope is not the witness proved by `exists_qldErr_le`; it is a distinct
calculation that still requires a dedicated formal theorem if it is to be
advertised as proved.

### Normalization and conclusion differences

Both comparisons use an **unsquared state norm** and, for each party and basis,
a **sum of squared operator-action norms**. There is no answer averaging and no
factor \(1/2\).

The answer maps differ. The public theorem uses `map rdPauliVec`, which sends
malformed answers to zero and thereby produces a completed answer family. The
local headline compares the raw effect of each prescribed Pauli answer directly
with the ideal projector. The two families agree on legally supported
strategies, but they are not definitionally the same for arbitrary strategies.

On a common encoding, if the state norm and completed-family operator distance
are both at most \(f=\operatorname{qldErr}\), the local raw-transfer calculation
gives

\[
 D_{\mathrm{raw}}\le2f+4f^2+344e\le104f,
\]

using \(4e\le f\le4\). This is a mathematical normalization calculation, not a
proved transport theorem between the two repositories.

The most useful scalar comparison is therefore:

| Bound | Polynomial parameter | Error exponent | Qualification |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Selected local canonical target | \(100\) | \(1/67108864\) | **NOT IMPLEMENTED**; raw prescribed-answer effects and fixed odd-extension field model |
| Public reconstructed proof witness | \(a_V\) above | \(1/2560000\) | Witness used by the public existential error-shape proof |
| Public sharper calculated envelope | \(10^{12}\) | \(1/1280000\) | Unformalized scalar calculation from the public definitions |

The public calculated exponent is \(52.4288\) times the selected local exponent,
while the selected local polynomial dependence is far smaller. Neither scalar
envelope dominates throughout the shared parameter domain.

### Regimes in which each side is smaller

Take \(m=1\), \(d=n\), \(e=0\), and \(q=2^{n+1}\), with \(n\) an even power
of two. These parameters lie in the shared field domain.

- At \(n=2^{50}\), the selected local canonical expression is below
  \(2^{-16772208}\), while the actual public `qldErr` equals \(4\). The
  public quantity \(L_V\) already forces \(H_V\ge1\).
- At \(n=2^{80}\), the public calculated envelope is below
  \(2^{-9.44\cdot10^{17}}\), while the selected local canonical expression has
  base-two logarithmic size about \(-1.80\cdot10^{16}\). In this regime the
  public calculated envelope is the smaller displayed bound.

These are extreme regimes used to compare asymptotic behavior, not practical
parameter recommendations. At fixed \(md\), reducing \(\varepsilon\) and
increasing \(q\) cannot remove the positive tail term \(2^{-bmd}\). Every
finite-\(md\) envelope therefore has a nonzero floor.

     2	
     3	> **Draft status, 2026-09-29.** This report records approved mathematical
     4	> calculations at repository commit
     5	> [`7bdfa416b7ff1f4a19de98b915efb3ca940f6fd9`][baseline-commit]. The two

    11	
    12	The main gains below concern powers and scaling, not only numerical
    13	coefficients. For a small number `x`, replacing `x^(1/40000)` by
    14	`x^(1/8192)` changes how quickly the error tends to zero. Replacing a factor
    15	`k^2 m^4` by `k^(1/4) m^(1/2)` changes how the estimate behaves as the test
    16	parameters grow. These changes are qualitatively different from replacing one
    17	fixed coefficient by a slightly smaller one.
    18	
    19	This distinction is especially important for the Pauli basis test. Its standard
    20	error function is
    21	
    22	```text
    23	deltaQld(a,b,epsilon,m,d,q)
    24	  = a (md)^a (epsilon^b + q^(-b) + 2^(-bmd)).
    25	```
    26	
    27	The same parameter `a` is both the leading coefficient and the polynomial
    28	degree. Absorbing a large numerical coefficient by increasing `a` can therefore
    29	turn a modest polynomial dependence into an enormous one. The selected QPBT
    30	calculation avoids that loss until the final canonical corollary.
    31	
    32	The LDT result is also an independent target. Its stronger conclusion is useful
    33	even apart from its later import into QPBT.
    34	
    35	## Notation and status convention
    36	
    37	For the QPBT discussion, write
    38	
    39	\[
    40	 e=\min(\varepsilon,1),\qquad n=md,\qquad r=\frac{n}{q},
    41	 \qquad E_b=e^b+q^{-b}+2^{-bn},
    42	\]
    43	
    44	and
    45	
    46	\[
    47	 \Delta_{a,b}(\varepsilon,m,d,q)
    48	 =a n^a\bigl(\varepsilon^b+q^{-b}+2^{-bn}\bigr).
    49	\]
    50	
    51	The report uses the following status terms.
    52	
    53	- **Baseline calculation** means that the number was reconstructed from the
    54	  checked-in proof at the pinned commit, but the dedicated fixed-constant
    55	  baseline theorem required for this project has not yet been verified.
    56	- **NOT IMPLEMENTED (selected; proof in progress)** means that the calculation
    57	  was selected for issues #728 or #729, but no completed declaration or merged
    58	  pull request is evidence for it yet.
    59	- **NOT IMPLEMENTED (deferred)** means that the idea remains outside the two
    60	  selected scopes.
    61	- **REJECTED** means that the proposed inference is unsupported or false for the
    62	  stated proof route; it is not an available improvement.
    63	
    64	## Part I: low individual degree test
    65	
    66	### Current baseline calculation
    67	
    68	The source theorem `thm:main-formal` states the final quantum soundness result
    69	for the low individual degree test. The paper prints the error
    70	
    71	\[
    72	 \boxed{
    73	 B_{\mathrm{LDT}}
    74	 =100000 k^2m^4\left(
    75	 \varepsilon^{1/40000}+(d/q)^{1/40000}
    76	 +\exp\!\left(-\frac{k}{2560000m^2}\right)
    77	 \right).}
    78	\]
    79	
    80	The same expression is the definition of `mainFormalError` in the pinned Lean
    81	tree, and `mainFormal` uses it for all three final consistency conclusions.
    82	Nevertheless, this report treats the unfolded expression as a **baseline
    83	calculation** until issue #728 supplies and verifies the assigned explicit
    84	baseline theorem.
    85	
    86	The current Lean domain must be kept unchanged. It assumes a projective
    87	two-space strategy passing with failure at most \(\varepsilon\), a field model,
    88	and
    89	
    90	\[
    91	 k\ge 400md,\qquad k>0.
    92	\]
    93	
    94	It does not assume \(\varepsilon\le1\), \(d\le q\), or \(k\le q\), and it
    95	includes \(d=0\). The paper prints only \(k\ge md\). The stronger Lean sampling
    96	condition and the nonzero boundary are documented in the
    97	[large-sampling correction][gap-k] and [zero-sampling correction][gap-zero].
    98	The selected theorem strengthens the conclusion on this current Lean domain; it
    99	does not restore the wider printed domain.

   107	 B_{\triangle}
   108	 =\min\!\left\{1,
   109	 10000 k^{1/4}m^{1/2}\left(
   110	 \varepsilon^{1/8192}+(d/q)^{1/8192}

   300	## Part II: quantum Pauli basis test
   301

   304	The source theorem `thm:pauli` and Lean theorem `pauli_soundness` assert the

   311	 c&=1024(172+\sqrt{344}),\\
   312	 t&=2(2c+4886363136+4),\\
   313	 Q&=10560(344+3t)+24t+11008,\\
   314	 L&=115\bigl(1+(16Q+8320)^{1/8}\bigr)+1,\\
   315	 H&=1+6(Q^{1/2}+L^{1/4}+Q^{1/4}+1),\\

   317	 \end{aligned}

## Comparison with the pinned public `qldErr`

### Source and domain

The benchmark is Thomas Vidick's public `MIPRE-formalization` at exact commit
[`286b3ca44f811fa6e37517c04981bc2f164ee6b5`][public-commit]. The inspected
mirror contained 398 manifested source files, all of whose hashes matched its
provenance record. The pinned repository license is
[Apache-2.0][public-license]. No benchmark code was copied, and no benchmark
build was run for this report.

The public theorem [`qld_soundness`][public-soundness] covers arbitrary POVM
strategies. The construction of the mirror witness is present in
[`MirrorExists.lean`][public-mirror], and the divisibility \(4m\mid q\) needed
inside the small-error regime is derived in [`Regime.lean`][public-regime]. An
earlier preliminary concern that either piece was missing is therefore
superseded. Likewise, a suspected square-root mismatch in `deltaLegs_comp` was a
parsing error; the proof and definition agree. Neither concern is a defect of
the public repository.

The public theorem ranges over arbitrary finite fields of characteristic two.
The local theorem uses the fixed admissible field model with \(q=2^\ell\) for
odd \(\ell\), \(d\ge1\), and \(m\mid q\). Numerical comparisons below are on
the shared domain.

### The actual capped composition

The public error is a composed function, not merely an existential slogan. With
the notation \(e,n,r\) above, define

\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_V&=2\sqrt{57676416e}+\sqrt{86e}+86e,\\
 D_V&=80Q_V+9228227936e,\\
 P_V&=D_V/2+\sqrt{D_V/2}
  +\sqrt{32D_V+4\sqrt{172e}+2(n+1)/q},\\
 T_V&=5m^2P_V+4Q_V+(n+1)/q,\\
 A_V^{\mathrm{CL}}&=2\cdot10^{11},
 \qquad B_V^{\mathrm{CL}}=1/40000,\\
 L_V&=A_V^{\mathrm{CL}}(4n)^{A_V^{\mathrm{CL}}}
 \left(T_V^{B_V^{\mathrm{CL}}}+q^{-B_V^{\mathrm{CL}}}
 +2^{-4B_V^{\mathrm{CL}}n}\right),\\
 U_V&=2L_V+115352832e,\\
 S_V&=2\sqrt{U_V}+2/q+8U_V,\\
 X_V&=72(10S_V+860e+2\sqrt{172e}+r),\\
 H_V&=2\sqrt{X_V}+2X_V,
 \qquad \eta_V=2-2\sqrt{1-H_V},\\
 F_V&=66S_V+44\sqrt{688e}+46r+1892e+13\sqrt{\eta_V}.
 \end{aligned}
\]

The definition in [`QLDError.lean`][public-qlderr] is

\[
 \operatorname{qldErr}(e,m,d,q)=
 \begin{cases}
 \min(F_V,4),&48n\le q\text{ and }H_V<1,\\
 4,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]

The component definitions occur in the public files
[`Combined.lean`][public-combined], [`Lines.lean`][public-lines],
[`PaddedLIDT.lean`][public-padded], the classical LDT
[`Parameters.lean`][public-lidt-parameters], [`SwapItemOne.lean`][public-swap-one],
and [`SwapItemTwo.lean`][public-swap-two].

### Existential witness and sharper calculated envelope

The public theorem [`exists_qldErr_le`][public-qlderr-witness] existentially
bounds `qldErr` by the same shape \(\Delta_{a,b}\). Reconstructing the witness
arithmetic used by that proof gives

\[
 b_V=\frac1{2560000}.
\]

If \(A=2\cdot10^{11}\) and

\[
 R=(A4^A+1)(A+9456574485125),
\]

then the traced coefficient parameter is

\[
 \boxed{a_V=10758960R+620538301950748.}
\]

It has \(\log_{10}a_V\approx120411998296.91\). These are reconstructed proof
witnesses, not numbers printed in the existential theorem.

A separate calculation from the definitions avoids the initial weakening
\(e\le e^{1/2}\) in the generic error-shape argument and gives the sharper
**unformalized scalar envelope**

\[
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{qldErr}(e,m,d,q)
 \le\min\!\left(4,\Delta_{10^{12},\,1/1280000}
   (\varepsilon,m,d,q)\right).}
\]

This envelope is not the witness proved by `exists_qldErr_le`; it is a distinct
calculation that still requires a dedicated formal theorem if it is to be
advertised as proved.

### Normalization and conclusion differences

Both comparisons use an **unsquared state norm** and, for each party and basis,
a **sum of squared operator-action norms**. There is no answer averaging and no
factor \(1/2\).

The answer maps differ. The public theorem uses `map rdPauliVec`, which sends
malformed answers to zero and thereby produces a completed answer family. The
local headline compares the raw effect of each prescribed Pauli answer directly
with the ideal projector. The two families agree on legally supported
strategies, but they are not definitionally the same for arbitrary strategies.

On a common encoding, if the state norm and completed-family operator distance
are both at most \(f=\operatorname{qldErr}\), the local raw-transfer calculation
gives

\[
 D_{\mathrm{raw}}\le2f+4f^2+344e\le104f,
\]

using \(4e\le f\le4\). This is a mathematical normalization calculation, not a
proved transport theorem between the two repositories.

The most useful scalar comparison is therefore:

| Bound | Polynomial parameter | Error exponent | Qualification |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Selected local canonical target | \(100\) | \(1/67108864\) | **NOT IMPLEMENTED**; raw prescribed-answer effects and fixed odd-extension field model |
| Public reconstructed proof witness | \(a_V\) above | \(1/2560000\) | Witness used by the public existential error-shape proof |
| Public sharper calculated envelope | \(10^{12}\) | \(1/1280000\) | Unformalized scalar calculation from the public definitions |

The public calculated exponent is \(52.4288\) times the selected local exponent,
while the selected local polynomial dependence is far smaller. Neither scalar
envelope dominates throughout the shared parameter domain.

### Regimes in which each side is smaller

Take \(m=1\), \(d=n\), \(e=0\), and \(q=2^{n+1}\), with \(n\) an even power
of two. These parameters lie in the shared field domain.

- At \(n=2^{50}\), the selected local canonical expression is below
  \(2^{-16772208}\), while the actual public `qldErr` equals \(4\). The
  public quantity \(L_V\) already forces \(H_V\ge1\).
- At \(n=2^{80}\), the public calculated envelope is below
  \(2^{-9.44\cdot10^{17}}\), while the selected local canonical expression has
  base-two logarithmic size about \(-1.80\cdot10^{16}\). In this regime the
  public calculated envelope is the smaller displayed bound.

These are extreme regimes used to compare asymptotic behavior, not practical
parameter recommendations. At fixed \(md\), reducing \(\varepsilon\) and
increasing \(q\) cannot remove the positive tail term \(2^{-bmd}\). Every
finite-\(md\) envelope therefore has a nonzero floor.

## Implementation pending

As of this draft, there are no proved before/after declaration pairs, merged
pull requests, or validation records for the two selected targets. The rows for
issues #728 and #729 must remain **NOT IMPLEMENTED (selected; proof in
progress)** until exact evidence exists.

Final integration must perform all of the following.

1. Record the actual fixed-constant LDT baseline declaration and the actual
   improved declaration merged for #728. Verify that both retain the full
   `mainFormal` hypotheses, including \(k\ge400md\), \(k>0\), \(d=0\), and
   the three conclusions for one common pair of projective polynomial
   measurements.
2. Replace the LDT calculation status by the **proved** before/after formulas
   only if the merged theorem has exactly those constants. Record the pull
   request, merge commit, axiom-audit entry, and focused and full validation
   actually run.
3. Record the actual fixed-witness QPBT baseline declaration merged for #729,
   including whether it uses \(a_0\) or the padded \(a_{\mathrm{base}}\). Do not
   conflate the two.
4. Record the actual improved QPBT declaration, canonical `deltaQld` corollary,
   and any qubit corollary. Verify that they retain arbitrary strategies, the
   nonnegative error domain, the raw prescribed-answer effects, the isometry
   range projections, and one common auxiliary state.
5. Replace the QPBT calculation status by the **proved** target only if the
   merged theorem establishes \(\min(4,10^{14}(md)^4E_{1/67108864})\), the
   canonical \(a=100\) form, or a precisely documented stronger bound. Record
   the exact declarations and pull request rather than suggested names from the
   analysis.
6. Add every new headline to the appropriate LDT or QPBT axiom audit, and record
   the exact audit commands, file checks, project build, local CI, and
   independent review results from the merged heads. This draft supplies none
   of that proof evidence.
7. Update both candidate tables from **NOT IMPLEMENTED** to **IMPLEMENTED** only

8. Keep the benchmark qualifications: no cross-repository raw-answer transport
   has been proved, the public calculated \((10^{12},1/1280000)\) envelope is

The principal remaining implementation risk is not an unresolved mathematical
selection. It is extracting fixed numerical witnesses from existential
interfaces and preserving the same measurements, auxiliary state, isometries,
and range projections through the stronger estimates.

+# Error bounds in the low individual degree and Pauli basis tests
+
+> **Draft status, 2026-09-29.** This report records approved mathematical
+> calculations at repository commit
+> [`7bdfa416b7ff1f4a19de98b915efb3ca940f6fd9`][baseline-commit]. The two
+> selected improvements are **not implemented** in this draft: the LDT proof is
+> in progress under issue [#728][issue-728], and the QPBT quantitative proof is
+> in progress under issue [#729][issue-729]. No declaration name, pull request,
+> validation result, or claim of a proved improved headline is inferred from
+> those issues.
+
+The main gains below concern powers and scaling, not only numerical
+coefficients. For a small number `x`, replacing `x^(1/40000)` by
+`x^(1/8192)` changes how quickly the error tends to zero. Replacing a factor
+`k^2 m^4` by `k^(1/4) m^(1/2)` changes how the estimate behaves as the test
+parameters grow. These changes are qualitatively different from replacing one
+fixed coefficient by a slightly smaller one.
+
+This distinction is especially important for the Pauli basis test. Its standard
+error function is
+
+```text
+deltaQld(a,b,epsilon,m,d,q)
+  = a (md)^a (epsilon^b + q^(-b) + 2^(-bmd)).
+```

+The same parameter `a` is both the leading coefficient and the polynomial
+degree. Absorbing a large numerical coefficient by increasing `a` can therefore
+turn a modest polynomial dependence into an enormous one. The selected QPBT
+calculation avoids that loss until the final canonical corollary.
+
+The LDT result is also an independent target. Its stronger conclusion is useful
+even apart from its later import into QPBT.
+
+## Notation and status convention
+
+For the QPBT discussion, write
+
+\[
+ e=\min(\varepsilon,1),\qquad n=md,\qquad r=\frac{n}{q},
+ \qquad E_b=e^b+q^{-b}+2^{-bn},
+\]
+
+and
+
+\[
+ \Delta_{a,b}(\varepsilon,m,d,q)
+ =a n^a\bigl(\varepsilon^b+q^{-b}+2^{-bn}\bigr).
+\]
+
+The report uses the following status terms.

+  checked-in proof at the pinned commit, but the dedicated fixed-constant

+- **NOT IMPLEMENTED (deferred)** means that the idea remains outside the two
+  selected scopes.

+  stated proof route; it is not an available improvement.
+
+## Part I: low individual degree test
+
+### Current baseline calculation
+
+The source theorem `thm:main-formal` states the final quantum soundness result
+for the low individual degree test. The paper prints the error
+
+\[
+ \boxed{

  1739		&= \E_{s} \sum_{a\in \F_q} \ketbra{a+s}{a} \otimes \ketbra{a+s}{a} \\

  1744	\[
  1745		\left \| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\| \leq \left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_X \ket{\vartheta} \right\| + \left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\|\;.

  1748	\[
  1749		\left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_W \ket{\vartheta} \right\|^2 = 1 - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} + \bra{\vartheta} H_W^2 \ket{\vartheta} \leq 2 - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} \leq \delta_S\;,

  1751	where in the inequality we used that $H_W \leq \Id$. Furthermore,
  1752	\begin{align*}
  1753		\bra{\vartheta} H_W^2 \ket{\vartheta} &=\| H_W \ket{\vartheta} \|^2\\
  1754		 &= \| \ket{\vartheta} + (H_W - \Id) \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \\

  1767		\bra{\vartheta} (\Id_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes (\proj{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''}) \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - 2\delta_S - \sqrt{\delta_S} \;.

  1770	\[
  1771		\ket{\aux_0}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} = (\bra{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''} \cdot \ket{\vartheta}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''}

  1815		\[
  1816			\tau^X(s) \tau^Z_h \tau^X(s)^\dagger = \tau^Z_{h + s} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \tau^Z(s) \tau^X_h \tau^Z(s)^\dagger = \tau^X_{h + s}~;

  1833		where in the last line we used that $(\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} = (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$.

  1837		&\approx_{md/q}  \E_u \sum_{\substack{h, h' : \\ g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)}} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-8} \\

  1839		&=  \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \, V_\alice^\dagger \, \otimes V_\bob  \, \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \, V_\bob^\dagger \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-9}

  1842		\begin{align*}
  1843			& \E_u \sum_{\substack{h \neq h' : \\ g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)}} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta}  \\

  1850		\begin{align*}
  1851			\text{\cref{eq:qld-unitary-9}} &\approx_{O(\delta_S^{1/4})} \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\hat{\psi}} M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1852			&\geq 1 - O(\delta_S^{1/2})\;,
  1853		\end{align*}
  1854	        where the last line comes from \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-5}.
  1855		Together with \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-7}, 
  1856		\[
  1857		\text{\cref{eq:qld-unitary-7}} \leq O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)\;.	
  1858		\]
  1859		This concludes the proof of the second item of the lemma.
  1860	\end{proof}
  1861	
  1862	We now prove \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}. 
  1863	\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}]
  1864		Let $\strategy = (\psi,M)$ be a projective strategy for $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeeds with probability at least $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi}$ is a bipartite state on registers $\alice \bob$. As mentioned at the beginning of \Cref{sec:commutation}, we assume that the state $\ket{\psi}$ is padded with sufficiently many ancilla $\ket{0}$ qubits. Let $\phi_\alice$ be the following isometry mapping the register $\alice$ to the registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ where $\alice'$ and $\alice''$ are isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$:
  1865		\[
  1866			\phi_\alice: \ket{\theta}_\alice \mapsto V_\alice (\ket{\theta}_\alice \otimes (\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice' \alice''})
  1867		\]
  1868		where $V_\alice$ is the unitary acting on $\alice \alice' \alice''$ from \Cref{lem:qld-unitary}. Define the isometry $\phi_\bob$ analogously. \Cref{lem:qld-unitary} then implies that there exists a state $\ket{\aux}$ on registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ such that
  1869		\[
  1870			\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_\bob \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} \right \|^2 \leq \delta_\qld
  1871		\]

  1873		\[
  1874			\phi_\alice \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\alice \, \phi_\alice^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \phi_\bob \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\bob \, \phi_\bob^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''}
  1875		\]
  1876		where the $\approx$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$.   1877	\end{proof}

Two useful mechanisms behind the larger remaining candidates are sufficiently concrete to investigate next:

- For complete POVMs define
  \[
  U(A)=\mathbb E_x\sum_a\langle A_a-A_a^2\rangle\ge0.

  The exact identity
  \[
  2\,\operatorname{Cons}(A,B)
   =\operatorname{DistSq}(A,B)+U(A)+U(B)
  \]
  combined with the three-step squared-norm triangle proves
  \(\operatorname{Cons}(A,D)\le3(\epsilon+\delta+\gamma)\).
  Completeness is load-bearing: do not apply this unchanged to submeasurements. With rounded \(P\) projective, the same identity gives
  \(\operatorname{Cons}(P,B)\le r+2\delta\) from
  \(\operatorname{DistSq}(P,A)\le r\) and
  \(\operatorname{Cons}(A,B)\le\delta\).
- In one-sided pasting, retaining the existing \(2\delta\) mirror estimate gives, for \(C=32\), an error bounded by
  \[
  2\delta+\sqrt{
   2C\delta+2\sqrt{2\delta}+2\delta+2\sqrt{C\delta}
   +2\eta+2\sqrt{4\delta+2\eta}+4\sqrt\delta}.
  \]
  On the unit square, the radicand is at most
  \(90\sqrt\delta+6\sqrt\eta\).
  Hence the whole expression is at most

  Outside the unit square use the independent consistency-defect cap \(1\).

Propagating the stronger consistency calculus through commutation, passing, and rounding, together with the pasting change, has a prospective sixteenfold exponent gain even before the recommended extraction change. That is a larger multi-module undertaking; its complete constants have not been reconstructed here. It should not be counted as an already available improved headline.

**Coverage, source integrity, and implementation cautions**

The survey traced the quantitative interfaces through Games, Observables, Combining, Extraction, Soundness, and QubitForm, including the relevant algebraic collision and exact-transport inputs. It also inspected quantum linearity and symmetrization to establish that they introduce no hidden headline loss. This is coverage of the quantitative dependency chain, not a claim that every helper proof in the 339 QPBT files was individually audited.

Several tempting “improvements” are invalid:

- The dimension factor in combined lines cannot simply be hidden inside `poly(m²ε,md/q)`. [`not_exists_combining_quarter_power_bound`](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ErrorObstruction.lean:37) gives a scalar obstruction.
- Conditional collision estimates require the actual nondegenerate sampling law and restoration of discarded mass.
- Pasting needs an additive error contract; the literal product interpretation has a documented counterexample.
- Symmetrization preserves a supplied strategy’s value exactly. The slack in the supremum-attainment statement cannot be removed by arithmetic.
- Magic Square rigidity’s agreement hypothesis is load-bearing. Neither smaller constants nor symmetry alone eliminates it.
- The inherited LDT theorem assumes \(N\ge400md\) and \(N>0\), stronger than the printed sampling condition. Both the existing and proposed auxiliary choices satisfy those assumptions internally.
- Preserve admissibility \(q=2^k\) with odd \(k\), \(d\ge1\), \(m\mid q\), and the fixed field model. No proposed headline needs an additional parameter hypothesis.
- Preserve the isometry range projections and raw prescribed-answer effects. Comparing only completed measurements would weaken the source-facing conclusion.

Relevant Mathlib support is already installed: `Real.rpow_add_le_add_rpow`, `Real.rpow_mul`, `Real.mul_rpow`, exponent monotonicity on both sides of one, `Real.sqrt_le_iff`, and inner-product norm-square identities. Most operator transport should reuse the project API rather than introduce new matrix infrastructure.

The principal remaining risk is formal engineering: fixed constants have been hidden by existential interfaces, several useful transfer lemmas are private, and all stronger headlines must be composed with internally constructed witnesses. Some extraction docstrings still describe formerly open compositions; the inspected `SourceUnitary` and final soundness proofs do perform those compositions.

Before claiming either improvement, prove the explicit baseline, add all new headlines and qubit forms to `Test/AxiomAudit.lean`, and validate the affected files followed by the required audit build. On \(\varepsilon>1\), a larger exponent is not automatically a pointwise smaller numerical expression; state the comparison on \(0\le\varepsilon\le1\), or additionally publish the bound evaluated at \(\min(\varepsilon,1)\).

Survey validation consisted of source inspection and independent arithmetic calculations. No proposed new bound was type-checked. No external benchmark repository was accessed; comparison remains with the independent benchmark worker.
If both recommendations are implemented and the improved one-coordinate LDT transport is used, the calculated Pauli exponent becomes

\[
\boxed{b_{\rm joint}=1/268{,}435{,}456=2^{-28},}
\]

a factor \(19.53125\) larger than the traced baseline exponent. Substituting \(c=1200,\tau=1/32768\) into the numerical recurrence above gives a mixed-transfer coefficient with \(\log_{10}a\approx735.942\); **\(a=10^{740}\)** is a conservative round-number candidate. These combined numbers require Lean verification and should not yet be advertised as proved.

**Significance ranking for main’s decision.**

| Rank | Candidate | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | LDT \(k^2m^4\to k^{1/16}m^{1/8}\), exponent \(1/40000\to1/32768\) | Largest independently derived native-LDT improvement; concrete scalar proof above; benefits QPBT through its import |
| 2 | Separate extraction state/operator errors | Eightfold Pauli exponent improvement and avoids two prefactor squarings; uses existing construction estimates |
| 3 | Preserve coefficient and polynomial degree separately throughout QPBT | Potentially enormous scaling improvement; existing \(m^5d^2\) transport demonstrates the opportunity, but propagation is broader than the two local changes above |
| 4 | LDT fallback \(75000k^2m^4\) with exponent \(1/32768\) | Lower-cost option already close to the existing cascade estimates; substantially weaker than rank 1 |
| 5 | Remove only the one-coordinate transport’s extra square root | Doubles the downstream exponent; useful consequence to include with rank 1 |
| 6 | Reduce full Magic Square rigidity’s \(2\cdot10^{12}\) | Useful for that theorem, but not a direct improvement to the current Pauli path |
| 7 | Improve induction’s \(1/1024\), replace projectivization, or remove dimension factors | Potentially significant, but requires new mathematical work; no established improvement from this survey |

Removing the extended-line dimension factor by scalar absorption is not justified. The repository proves a numerical obstruction in [not_exists_combining_quarter_power_bound](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ErrorObstruction.lean:37). This obstructs the proposed absorption argument; it is not a counterexample to every possible stronger strategy theorem.

For a proposed QPBT bound \(\Delta_{a,b}<1\), a sufficient parameter regime is

\[
\varepsilon<(3an^a)^{-1/b},\qquad
q>(3an^a)^{1/b},\qquad
bn>\log_2(3an^a).
\]

Thus neither a larger exponent nor a finite explicit coefficient alone establishes practical nontriviality. The \(2^{-bn}\) term prevents arbitrarily large \(q\) and arbitrarily small \(\varepsilon\) from rescuing a fixed small \(md\). The current and proposed canonical coefficients still imply extremely large nontrivial regimes.

The additive implementation sequence should be:

1. Prove explicit baseline siblings of the affected headlines, exposing the numerical witnesses above. Preserve all existing statements.
2. Add `mainFormal_quantitative` with the \(200k^{1/16}m^{1/8}\) envelope and the same three conclusions and hypotheses.
3. Add an explicit one-coordinate transport and componentwise extraction/transfer lemmas, then a new explicit Pauli headline.
4. Add every new headline to [Test/AxiomAudit.lean](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean:79), retaining all existing audit declarations.

The remaining uncertainties are the formal verification of the numerical candidates, the breadth of explicit-witness threading, and the unavailable pinned benchmark. The public `qldErr` formula, its exact domain and normalization, the full benchmark SHA, and its pinned license still need retrieval before publishing a side-by-side comparison. Approximately 17 minutes had elapsed at the last timestamp check; dispatcher telemetry is authoritative for final time and token cost.

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$ROOT"
HOOK_ROOT="$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
GIT_LOCAL_ENV_VARS="$(git rev-parse --local-env-vars)"

run_without_git_local_env() (
  # Git exports repository-local variables while running hooks.  Several script
  # tests create temporary repositories; keep those tests independent of this
  # checkout.
  unset $GIT_LOCAL_ENV_VARS
  "$@"
)

# A merge commit can be syntactically valid while its index has been reset to
# the first-parent tree.  That failure mode silently discarded clean incoming
# additions on issue-109 and issue-110 (issue #222).  Check the pending index
# before every other gate, including the documented blanket hook bypass: a
# missing incoming path is valid only when the branch deleted a base path.
MERGE_HEAD_PATH="$(git rev-parse --git-path MERGE_HEAD)"
if [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking the merge result for silent incoming loss."
  python3 "$HOOK_ROOT/local/bin/merge_loss_guard.py" --repo "$ROOT"
fi

# Scope-control guard (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-01, the issue-0007 overbuild):
# workflow scaffolding is budgeted at <=1000 changed lines per commit (400 until the owner raised it on 2026-09-05).  This is
# mechanical enforcement — repeated verbal correction of scaffolding bloat did
# not stick, so the budget lives in the hook.  The override env var is granted
# only after a recorded main decision, never self-granted by a worker session. Runs
# before the ACMR early-exit so deletion-only commits are counted too
# (numstat includes deletions; PR 7 round 3, F8), and before the
# MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS exit so a blanket hook skip cannot launder the
# workflow budget override.
# A merge that carries main stages already-reviewed content.  A merge head
# contained in github/main measures the budget against MERGE_HEAD; a merge head
# that contains github/main (a parent branch of a stack that already merged
# main; owner decision 2026-09-05) measures it against github/main, so inherited
# main content counts zero while the PR's cumulative workflow diff and any
# side-branch content beyond main still count.  Any other side-branch merge
# stays budgeted against HEAD.
if [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ] &&
    git merge-base --is-ancestor MERGE_HEAD refs/remotes/github/main 2>/dev/null; then
  BUDGET_BASE="$(git rev-parse MERGE_HEAD)"
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: main-history merge; budget measured against MERGE_HEAD."
elif [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ] &&
    git merge-base --is-ancestor refs/remotes/github/main MERGE_HEAD 2>/dev/null; then
  BUDGET_BASE="$(git rev-parse refs/remotes/github/main)"
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: non-main merge carrying github/main; workflow-layer content beyond github/main is budgeted."
else
  BUDGET_BASE=""
  if [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ]; then
    echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: non-main merge; workflow-layer merge content is budgeted."
  fi
fi
INFRA_CHANGED="$(git diff --cached --numstat $BUDGET_BASE -- local/ .githooks/ \
  scripts/tests/test_dispatch.py scripts/tests/test_github_workflow.py \
  scripts/tests/test_lake_root.py scripts/tests/test_pre_push_hook.py \
  scripts/tests/test_ready_packets.py scripts/tests/test_merge_loss_guard.py \
  | awk '{added=$1; deleted=$2; if (added != "-") total+=added+deleted} END {print total+0}')"
if [ "${INFRA_CHANGED:-0}" -gt 1000 ] && [ "${MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE:-}" != "1" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: staged workflow-layer change is ${INFRA_CHANGED} lines (budget: 1000)."
  echo "Scope control (local/personas/main.md): the budget is PER EPISODE, not per"
  echo "commit — serial oversized commits are the same violation and show in the"
  echo "telemetry. Shrink the change, or stop for a recorded main decision that"
  echo "authorizes MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE=1; workers must not self-grant it."
  exit 1
fi

if [ "${MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS:-}" = "1" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit hook skipped by MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1."
  exit 0
fi

STAGED_FILES="$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR)"
if [ -z "$STAGED_FILES" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking staged whitespace."
# Paper mirrors under references/ are byte-faithful captures of external
# arXiv sources (see references/*/README.md); their inherited trailing
# whitespace is part of the fidelity claim and must not be "fixed", so they
# are exempt from the whitespace gate (local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md,
# 2026-08-30).
git diff --cached --check -- ':(exclude)references/'

if printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_FILES" | grep -Eq '^scripts/(.*\.py|tests/.*)$'; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: running scripts/tests unit tests."
  run_without_git_local_env python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py'
fi

if printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_FILES" | grep -Eq \
  '^(blueprint/src/.*\.(tex|sty|cls)|scripts/(check_blueprint_latex|tex_utils)\.py|scripts/tests/test_check_blueprint_latex\.py|\.githooks/pre-commit)$'; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking blueprint LaTeX conventions."
  python3 scripts/check_blueprint_latex.py --root blueprint/src
fi

if ! printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_FILES" | grep -Eq \
  '^(MIPStarRE/|MIPStarRE\.lean|blueprint/src/|blueprint/lean_decls|scripts/(audit_new_proof_obligation_metadata|audit_paper_facing_proof_debt|audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses|audit_unfaithful_markers|audit_lean_axiom_declarations|check_blueprint_latex|check_paper_gap_note_style|check_statement_paper_origin|check_source_statement_changes|blueprint_lean_sync|lean_header_utils|tex_utils)\.py|docs/(CONTRIBUTING|project_conventions|anti_patterns|blueprint_style_guide|formalization-patterns|proof_frontier_review)\.md|docs/paper-gaps/|\.github/(actions|prompts|workflows)/|AGENTS\.md)'; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: no statement-integrity files staged."
  exit 0
fi

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking changed paper-gap note structure."
python3 scripts/check_paper_gap_note_style.py --root . --staged --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking statement-like paper-origin citations."
python3 scripts/check_statement_paper_origin.py --root .

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking new proof-obligation metadata."
python3 scripts/audit_new_proof_obligation_metadata.py --root . --staged --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking paper-facing proof-debt headers."
echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: do not close proof gaps by adding non-paper bridge/package hypotheses."
python3 scripts/audit_paper_facing_proof_debt.py --root . --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking conclusion-shaped hypotheses."
python3 scripts/audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses.py --root . --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking unfaithful-dependency markers."
python3 scripts/audit_unfaithful_markers.py --root . --ci

python3 scripts/audit_lean_axiom_declarations.py --root . --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: ok."
